en.title: ui in pui (chicken / you put)
en.summary: This item illustrates the Romanian diphthong ui as found in the word pui.

sections.title: The sound ui
paragraphs: The letters ui sound as /uj/. Their main sound appears in (pui) /puj/, which means chicken or youth. This letter pair has two sounds in Romanian.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, round your lips tightly. Glide quickly to a sharp sound while spreading your lips wide. For the second sound, make two distinct beats. First push your lips forward into a small circle. Then shift your tongue high and forward for a clear separate sound. Touch your throat to feel steady voicing throughout.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: The letters ui make the single gliding sound /uj/ within one syllable, as in (puiul) /ˈpu.jul/. They split into two separate vowel beats /u.i/ across syllables, as heard in (ruină) /ruˈi.nə/ and (construit) /kon.struˈit/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn this pair into the single vowel of English fruit or juice. You must pronounce both elements clearly. In a single syllable, slide smoothly from the first sound to the second without stopping. Across two syllables, keep each vowel fully independent and never drop either sound.
